anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Barley loaves in John; Origen assigns wheat to five and barley to seven — not silently corrected.

pass_a_gloss: And perhaps the gospel too knows the same difference, whenever the Savior feeds those following him not from like loaves but from different: for some of them he breaks five of wheat, for others seven of barley, so that as many as cannot partake of Christ as of a purer and wheat loaf, because they still turn about beastlike and not yet rationally, may partake as of barley.
pass_b_english: And perhaps the gospel too knows the same difference, when the Savior feeds those who follow him not from like loaves but from different ones. For some of them he breaks five of wheat, and for others seven of barley — so that those who cannot [partake of Christ as of a purer wheat loaf, because they still live in a beastlike way and not yet rationally, may partake as of barley.]
source_text: Τάχα δὲ καὶ τὸ εὐαγ[γέ]λιον τὴν αὐτὴν διαφορὰν οἶδεν, ὅταν ὁ σ(ωτ)ὴρ τοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας αὐτῷ χορτάζῃ οὐκ ἐξ ἄρτων ὁμοίων ἀλλὰ διαφόρων· τοῖς μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν σιτίνους κατακλᾷ πέντε, τοῖς δὲ κριθίνους ἑπτά, ἵνα ὅσοι οὐ δύ||[νανται ὡς ἄρτου καθαρωτέρου καὶ σιτίνου μεταλαβεῖν τοῦ Χ(ριστο)ῦ διὰ τὸ κτηνωδῶς καὶ μήπω λογικῶς ἀναστρέφεσθαι μεταλάβωσιν ὡς κριθίνου.
